author: Haiku critic
text: The Delete ToolbarButton is declared variant="danger", but its recorded colour (oklch(0.62 0.013 264)) is the same neutral grey as the other verbs, so the danger variant shows no difference. The bulk bar Delete is a plain text button and the row context menu's Delete task... is danger. Decide whether destructive Delete should be visibly distinct, and apply the same treatment in all three places.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory leaves open whether Delete opens a confirmation, yet the feature list includes F07-033 Bulk delete confirmation and F07-034 Bulk delete toast. The inspector Delete and the bulk bar Delete should therefore show a confirmation before deleting. On desktop this is a separate sheet window with no backdrop dimming, and on web it is a modal dialog.

author: Haiku critic
text: The header Clear selection IconButton and the bulk bar text Clear both clear the selection, but the inventory gives different widget styles and says the header control lands on task-list only by inference. Use one Clear control, or document one landing behaviour for both, so the user does not see two different outcomes for the same action.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title-bar window controls (Close, Minimize, Full Screen) and the drag grip beside the project switcher are desktop window chrome. The web version runs in a browser tab and has no equivalent, so these should not be rebuilt there. Keep them only in the desktop build.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory says the bulk verbs call bulkSetDone, bulkMove, bulkCopy and bulkDelete with no failure handling recorded, and feature F07-025 states that bulk set done has no rollback on failure. In a multi-user cloud app these calls go to a server, so the web build needs a rollback or an error message for each bulk verb, and the shared list should be reconciled after a failed call.

node: widget:IconButton (subtask counter chevron, Task list pane)
author: Haiku critic
text: The chevron_left icon beside the '1 / 3' subtask counter is listed as present but not visible in the shot, and its purpose is marked as inferred. Feature F07-099 names an expand chevron on the subtask count badge, so the inventory needs to confirm whether the chevron exists and what it toggles. Without that it is unclear whether the parent row can collapse its subtasks from the list.
